column1: # Vendor documentation pages this package cites, and what each one DID when a person read
# it. Checked by `script/check_doc_sources.sh`; see that script's header for why this is
# status-and-destination rather than a content diff, and why a redirect is the signal.
#   url  expect_status  expect_location  observed_on  class  note
# `expect_location` is `-` when the page does not redirect. It is never left blank: TAB is
# IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses into one delimiter and every later column
# `class` is `auto` (a machine can verify this) or `manual` (it cannot — a human must
# re-read it, and the row goes STALE past 180 days to force that).
# Do not edit a row to make the check pass. The row records what someone READ; rewriting
# it to match a fetch nobody looked at turns this file into a rubber stamp.

column6: The portal root. Anonymous readers get 403; everything below needs a signed-in session. This venue is the family's proof that a monitor assuming public documentation covers zero percent of the venues that need it most — and that the ones behind a login are disproportionately the brokerages, where being wrong moves real money.

The product this package implements. Its two OpenAPI documents are committed under `openapi/` because they are fetched at runtime from a gateway on a different origin — a saved page carries the outline and not the specification.
The 17 User Guides committed under `user-guides/`, including the OAuth flow.

App registration and key management. NOTE, and it constrains any re-capture: the portal's `api-specification` endpoint returns the signed-in account's live `appKey` and `appSecret` in the same JSON as the specification, because that endpoint also feeds the "Try it" console. Redact BEFORE storing, never after.
